item.title: The Basics of Birding — Tue Aug 18, 7:30 AM — NJ
item.description: Are you just getting into birding or need a refresher? Then spend the day with Director Brett Ewald in the field learning the basics! This all-encompassing workshop combines in the field experience and id tips with discussions on bird families, occurrence/migration, optics, field guides, backyard birding/gardening and more. We’ll visit several local hotspots to take in warblers, kingbirds, shorebirds, terns, and other early migrants. Geared towards beginners and those wishing to improve their knowledge and appreciation of birds and birding, helping you take it to the next level! We don’t pre-set an itinerary but will visit those parts of Cape May that regularly hold good numbers of birds at this time of year. Final location decisions will be made by the leader, based on local knowledge and conditions at the time. item.title: Let's Walk!! Garret Mountain — Sat Aug 22, 9:30 AM
item.description:
Let's Walk!! Join me for the 5K paved loop at Garret Mountain Reservation. We will meet at the parking lot on the loop, turn right on Park Ave from Mountain Ave, lot is on the left. GPS Address for Garrett is 8 Mountain Ave Woodland Park.
Garret Mountain Reservation, located in both Woodland Park and Paterson, is one of Passaic County’s most frequented parks. The original landscape was designed by the famed Olmsted Brothers Firm. The 310 acres of recreational space sits more than 500 feet above sea level, with scenic views of Paterson and the New York City skyline. Lambert Castle and Lambert Tower, two of Passaic County’s historic sites, are also located within Garret Mountain Reservation.
Rain or extreme weather will cancel the event.
Collaborative walk with "Montclair Women Over 50."
Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap.
Source: Meetu

item.description:

Remember The Titans (2000) | PG
In Virginia, high school football is a way of life, an institution revered, each game celebrated more lavishly than Christmas, each playoff distinguished more grandly than any national holiday. And with such recognition, comes powerful emotions. In 1971 high school football was everything to the people of Alexandria. But when the local school board was forced to integrate an all black school with an all white school, the very foundation of football's great tradition was put to the test. Watch the trailer here.

item.title: Art Lounge: Collage Night — Thu Aug 13, 7:00 PM
item.description:
Pull up a chair, get a cup of tea, and make something beautiful! Art Lounge is your laid-back Thursday night creative escape — no agenda, no pressure, no experience needed. Just good music, great company, and a table full of materials waiting to become something entirely your own. Cut, tear, layer, and arrange your way through the evening at whatever pace feels right. Not sure where to start? We’ve got prompts to spark your imagination and get the ideas flowing. Or ignore them completely and follow your instincts – either way works perfectly here. Bring your friends, bring your BYOB, and leave with a piece of art you actually made. It’s the best kind of Thursday night. 🗓 Thursday, August 13 | 7:00 pm – 8:30 pm 📍 The Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, 2nd Floor, Montclair, NJ 🎟 $10 | All materials provided | BYOB welcome Open to everyone. item.title: UNRECYCLABLE: Look Again - Assemblage Art Exhibit Opening — Fri Aug 14, 5:00 PM
item.description: UNRECYCLABLE: Look Again – Assemblage Art by Andrew Borg Opening Reception: Friday, August 14, 5 – 8pm The Space presents Unrecyclable: Look Again, a solo exhibition of assemblage art by Andrew Borg composed predominantly of the unrecyclable plastics, foams, and composites he refused to throw away for nearly two years — the molded trays, caps, and packaging inserts that carry no recycling code and vanish into the trash without a thought. The exhibition, culminating Borg’s year as Artist in Residence at The Space, is on view August 14–22, 2026, with an opening reception Friday, August 14, from 5 to 8pm. What began as an act of defiance gradually became an act of appreciation: these are highly engineered, purpose-built objects, molded to cushion, position, and protect — aesthetic objects in their own right, designed by someone, meant to be forgotten by everyone. item.title: Assemblage Lab & Gallery Talk with Andrew Borg — Sat Aug 22, 1:00 PM
item.description: Assemblage Lab & Gallery Talk with Andrew Borg Closing Event for “Unrecyclable: Look Again” What do you see when you really look at what you throw away? Join artist Andrew Borg for the closing event of Unrecyclable: Look Again — an afternoon that begins with a gallery talk and ends with your hands deep in materials you never thought twice about discarding. After walking through the exhibition and sharing the story behind his two-year collection of unrecyclable plastics, foams, and composites, Borg leads an immersive hands-on Assemblage Lab in which participants get to experience the process firsthand. Using unrecyclable packaging, abandoned electronics, appliances, and other “ghost objects,” you’ll build your own assemblage, sculpture, or mixed-media artwork — guided by the same impulse that drove this exhibition: look again. item.description:
